testing_gaps: CollaborationApiIntegrationTest covers sequential revocation and same-second rebinding, but not concurrent unbind with publication or acknowledge/close. The new relation, notification and event locking interactions therefore lack real-MySQL concurrency coverage for the immediate-revocation contract.
The MySQL fixtures use a single test transaction and do not cover simultaneous independent queueAbnormalEvent calls or cross-transaction deduplication.
No supplied frontend test covers navigation or filter changes during pending requests, where generation guards must prevent stale authorization data from reappearing.

findings.title: Cover closure before family alert publication
findings.suggested_fix: Add a real-MySQL integration case that creates an authorized pending family notification, acknowledges and closes the event before publish, invokes delivery.publish, then asserts CANCELLED, no sentAt, and a still-CLOSED event.

findings.title: Exercise authorization loss between detail requests
findings.suggested_fix: Add a page-level test with controlled GET and POST responses: resolve GET with a family message, return 403 from read, and assert the body remains absent while the authorization error appears; include a successful two-request case.

testing_gaps: Expiry fanout concurrent with unbind and same-second rebind needs independent-transaction MySQL verification. Existing rebind coverage is sequential within one test transaction; whether UPDATE JOIN/gap/event locks prevent stale family notification insertion after cancellation remains unresolved. No failing interleaving was established.

findings.title: Re-entering during a pending action can leave stale inbox state
findings.suggested_fix: Track in-flight read-all and family-event mutation promises independently of page generation. On page show, wait for a pending mutation before loading, or trigger a fresh load after that mutation settles if the page is visible; preserve generation checks for stale response rendering.

testing_gaps: The transactional MySQL integration tests and mocked dispatcher tests do not exercise a real publication rollback followed by failure bookkeeping in a separate committed transaction.
